messages:
alex: New engineer hit two rough DX things during first-run: redwoodctl installer left a profile with 600 perms that my user can't read (wtf), and local-test in our CI started blocking on a device-code flow.

alex: Repro steps: fresh macOS (ventura), `brew install redwoodctl`, `redwoodctl init --profile dev`, `redwoodctl local-test --mount ./seed:/srv/seed --debug`. redwoodctl v0.29.4.

mei: Oof. What do you mean by unreadable profile? `ls -la ~/.redwood`?

alex: `ls -la ~/.redwood` shows `config` owned by root with 0600. Installer logs show a failure mid-write and a retry that chowned to root. The CLI then warns but continues creating a "dev (partial)" profile.

ops-bot: Installer audit: installer v0.29.4 used temp file write without fsync on macOS. Race with updater could cause temp ownership to be wrong. Known class of bug. See infra issue #4002.

mei: Workaround: `sudo chown $(id -u):$(id -g) ~/.redwood/config && redwoodctl profiles repair`. We'll add an atomic-write patch.

alex: Thanks — that fixed the config/read error locally. Now the CI hang: job logs show `auth: refresh failed (401), starting device code flow` and then nothing. CI runner is noninteractive so there's no browser.

mei: We shouldn't launch interactive flows in noninteractive envs. Which CI provider?

alex: GitHub Actions self-hosted runner. We already set `CI=true` in jobs. But redwoodctl doesn't check it. It printed the device code URL and waited.

mei: Short-term fix: issue a token and export `REDWOOD_TOKEN` in the job. Example:
```
- name: Login service account
  run: | 
    redwoodctl auth login --service-account-key "$SA_KEY" --output token > /tmp/rw_token
    echo "REDWOOD_TOKEN=$(cat /tmp/rw_token)" >> $GITHUB_ENV
```
Then run `redwoodctl local-test`.

This prevents the device flow.

alex: That made CI fail fast on the mount instead of hanging (better). The mount is also empty in CI; suspicious. I tried absolute path and `realpath` but dind runner still shows empty dir.

ops-bot: Mount empties in dind are usually path sharing config or symlink issues. If your workspace is a symlink (eg /home/runner -> /mnt/ssd/runner) the nested Docker daemon may see a different host path. Try `docker run --rm -v $(realpath ./seed):/check busybox ls /check` in the CI job to verify.

alex: That `docker run` returned files, but `redwoodctl local-test` still sees empty. It looks like redwoodctl rewrites the mount path into the inner runtime (it uses an internal shim), so the path translation differs.

mei: We should add `REDWOOD_LOCAL_MOUNTS` env var that forces exact passthrough of specific host paths into the runtime, and add `REDWOOD_AUTH_MODE=noninteractive` so CLI errors out instead of starting device flow. I'll file infra tasks for both.

installer-bot: Filed infra#4003: add atomic writes for installer. Filed infra#4004: REDWOOD_AUTH_MODE + noninteractive failure. Filed infra#4005: REDWOOD_LOCAL_MOUNTS passthrough.

alex: Filed gist with minimal repro + `docker inspect` dumps: https://gist.github.com/alex/3f2b1c. Also attached CI job id 99231.

ci-bot: Rerun scheduled for job 99231 with pre-auth token.

mei: Followups: 1) installer atomic write patch (high); 2) CLI change to respect CI/noninteractive and exit nonzero if device flow required; 3) doc note for contributors about dind mounts and symlinked homes; 4) add integration test in infra that runs local-test inside dind and checks mount contents.

alex: Thanks folks — will add the docs note and a tiny smoke test in our repo. :thumbsup:
